statement: Cejel #638's v27 A1 reader credited a pytest hook with putting the collected items back when its list reading ended restored, treating every statement it did not model as harmless. Review found nine shapes where pytest ran no test yet the note said the items were back: a slice after the restore, a clear after a triple-quoted string (body end measured by raw indentation), sorted() as a copy, another name for the list, async or decorated closures, a helper redefined under if, a shadowed list, exec or an f-string field. Rules: when a reader must prove a safe outcome over arbitrary code, credit it only for a body made entirely of recognised statements; any other statement goes to a named not-read outcome. Tokenise the source as the language does before measuring where a block ends. Real restores outside the allowlist then move to the named outcome, which costs wording, never a false claim.

In the red-first commit of cejel's v27 A1 allowlist round, two fixtures for nested conftest.py scope expected A1's note to name a restoring hook in one conftest.py while another conftest.py's clearing hook rated every file hollow. A1 names a withheld rule only for a file that no rule moved (since #626 item C), so the note never names a hook that withholds nothing, and those two expectations could not pass under any correct implementation. They were red for the wrong reason, and the fix commit had to correct them. Three other new blocker fixtures were already green at the base and were kept only as regression pins. Rules: before committing a red fixture, check its expected output against the reporting rules already in force, not only against the new item's intent. After the red run, list which fixtures failed and why, and name the ones that passed at the base in the commit message.
